newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares plunge 6.31 percent at close.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares plunge 6.31 percent at close.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index plunged on Wednesday due in part to rumours that Beijing plans to crack down on mainland Chinese illegally buying B shares, brokers said.
The B index dived 8.53 points, or 6.31 percent, to close at 126.61, with turnover falling to HK$241.08 million from Tuesday's HK$415.10 million.

Brokers said the fall was due in part to rumours that Beijing plans to tighten controls on domestic investors buying B shares. A spokesman for the China Securities Regulatory Commission declined comment.

Despite a ban on mainland Chinese buying B shares, they can easily enter the market, brokers said. Shenzhen B shares are denominated in Hong Kong dollars which are easily available in the city, which borders Hong Kong.

Profit-taking contributed to the retreat after the index had gained about 50 percent over the past few sessions, brokers said. Investors will adopt a wait-and-see attitude in the coming sessions, one broker said.
SEG was the worst performer, down HK$0.49 to HK$3.80 on volume of 1.86 million shares. Southern Glass fell HK$0.55 to HK$4.60 on trade of 798,799 shares.
Changan Automobile traded the most on volume of 12.28 million shares and fell HK$0.22 to HK$2.99. Dadonghai shed HK$0.29 to HK$2.85, with 5.43 million shares traded.
Huafa, the sole gainer, edged up HK$0.13 to HK$3.68, with 324,400 shares changing hands, due to speculative buying.
The A market edged lower as investors cautiously reduced their positions after the recent bull run, brokers said.

The A index lost 7.85 points, or 1.73 percent, to 444.66 on turnover of 11.09 billion yuan, compared with 15.77 billion the previous session. The composite index ended down 8.18 points, or 1.92 percent, at 416.85.
Floppy disk maker Huayuan, the biggest loser, fell 0.62 yuan, or 5.59 percent, to 10.48 due to profit-taking, brokers said.
Chemical fibre maker Hainan Sea Rainbow ended down 0.65 yuan, or 5.38 percent, at 11.44 yuan.
Hotelier Shijiazhuang International was the star on speculative demand, brokers said. The counter advanced 2.68 yuan, or 14.16 percent, to 21.60 yuan.
